papers.title: TEMPO: Scaling Test-time Training for Large Reasoning Models
alternate_titles: TEMPO: Scaling Test-time Training for Large Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Test-time training (TTT) adapts model parameters on unlabeled test instances during inference time, which continuously extends capabilities beyond the reach of offline training. Despite initial gains, existing TTT methods for LRMs plateau quickly and do not benefit from additional test-time compute. Without external calibration, the self-generated reward signal increasingly drifts as the policy model evolves, leading to both performance plateaus and diversity collapse. We propose TEMPO, a TTT framework that interleaves policy refinement on unlabeled questions with periodic critic recalibration on a labeled dataset. By formalizing this alternating procedure through the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, we reveal that prior methods can be interpreted as incomplete variants that omit the crucial recalibration step. Reintroducing this step tightens the evidence lower bound (ELBO) and....

papers.title: TAGARELA - A Portuguese Speech Dataset from Podcasts
alternate_titles: TAGARELA - A Portuguese Speech Dataset from Podcasts
papers.abstract: Despite significant advances in speech processing, Portuguese remains under-resourced due to the scarcity of public, large-scale, and high-quality datasets. To address this gap, we present a new dataset, named TAGARELA, composed of over 8,972 hours of podcast audio, specifically curated for training automatic speech recognition (ASR) and text-to-speech (TTS) models. Notably, its scale rivals English’s GigaSpeech (10kh), enabling state-of-the-art Portuguese models. To ensure data quality, the corpus was subjected to an audio pre-processing pipeline and subsequently transcribed using a mixed strategy: we applied ASR models that were previously trained on high-fidelity transcriptions generated by proprietary APIs, ensuring a high level of initial accuracy. Finally, to validate the effectiveness of this new resource, we present ASR and TTS models trained exclusively on our dataset and evalua...

papers.title: T-Mimi: A Transformer-Based Mimi Decoder for Real-Time On-Phone TTS
alternate_titles: T-Mimi: A Transformer-Based Mimi Decoder for Real-Time On-Phone TTS
papers.abstract: Neural audio codecs provide promising acoustic features for speech synthesis, with representative streaming codecs like Mimi providing high-quality acoustic features for real-time Text-to-Speech (TTS) applications. However, Mimi’s decoder, which employs a hybrid transformer and convolution architecture, introduces significant latency bottlenecks on edge devices due to the the compute intensive nature of deconvolution layers which are not friendly for mobile-CPUs, such as the most representative framework XNNPACK [1]. This paper introduces T-Mimi, a novel modification of the Mimi codec decoder that replaces its convolutional components with a purely transformer-based decoder, inspired by the TS3-Codec architecture. This change dramatically reduces on-device TTS latency from 42.1ms to just 4.4ms. Furthermore, we conduct quantization aware training and derive a crucial finding: the final tw...

papers.title: SmoothCLAP: Soft-Target Enhanced Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining for Affective Computing
alternate_titles: SmoothCLAP: Soft-Target Enhanced Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining for Affective Computing
papers.abstract: The ambiguity of human emotions poses several challenges for machine learning models, as they often overlap and lack clear delineating boundaries. Contrastive language-audio pretraining (CLAP) has emerged as a key technique for generalisable emotion recognition. However, as conventional CLAP enforces a strict one-to-one alignment between paired audio–text samples, it overlooks intra-modal similarity and treats all non-matching pairs as equally negative. This conflicts with the fuzzy boundaries between different emotions. To address this limitation, we propose SmoothCLAP, which introduces softened targets derived from intra-modal similarity and paralinguistic features. By combining these softened targets with conventional contrastive supervision, SmoothCLAP learns embeddings that respect graded emotional relationships, while retaining the same inference pipeline as CLAP. Experiments on ei...

papers.title: Sing2Song: An Accompaniment Generation System Based on Solo Singing
alternate_titles: Sing2Song: An Accompaniment Generation System Based on Solo Singing
papers.abstract: AI has revolutionized music creation by enabling systems to accompany solo singing with polished instrumental accompaniments. However, existing methods such as SingSong [1] and FastSAG [2] struggle to process long singing inputs and offer limited control over genre, intro length, and other music parameters that are essential to accommodating user preferences. To this end, we propose Sing2Song, a hybrid accompaniment generation system that accepts solo singing audio and produces fully orchestrated accompaniment. The system comprises three core modules: (1) data-driven music information retrieval (MIR) models specifically trained using solo singing, including singing voice transcription (SVT), dynamic beat tracking, and music structure segmentation; (2) rule-based multi-track MIDI accompaniment generation; and (3) rule-based adaptive audio synthesis. This combination ensures both the accur...

papers.title: Short-Lived High-Volume Bandits
alternate_titles: Short-Lived High-Volume Bandits
papers.abstract: When Thousands of Items Arrive Every Hour: A New Approach to Online Experimentation Researchers have reported a new approach to address a key challenge for online platforms. In a new paper in Operations Research, Jia et al. introduced the Short-lived High-volume Bandits (SLHVB) framework. This models modern platforms where thousands of items—such as ads, stories, or interface designs—arrive each hour but remain available only briefly. The study develops a near-optimal online learning policy that balances exploration and exploitation. Theoretical analysis shows the algorithm achieves nearly the minimal possible loss as the number of user impressions grows. The team tested the policy in a large-scale field experiment with Glance, a leading lock-screen content platform. The policy increased viewing duration by 4.32% and click-through rates by 7.48% compared to the platform’s existing deep-l...

papers.title: Seaf: Semantic-Aware Frame Selection for Long-form Video Understanding
alternate_titles: Seaf: Semantic-Aware Frame Selection for Long-form Video Understanding
papers.abstract: While recent advances in multimodal large language models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in image-language reasoning tasks, their performance is often hampered when applied to long videos. Traditional frame selection methods mainly rely on uniform sampling, which is inherently inflexible. In this work, we propose Seaf, a semantic-aware frame sampling framework designed specifically for long-form video understanding via MLLMs. Unlike traditional uniform sampling methods, Seaf adaptively selects key frames that are relevant to the question from the entire video sequence. Notably, our method is fully training-free and parameter-free, making it highly compatible with any existing MLLM architecture as a plug-and-play module. Extensive experiments on multiple MLLMs demonstrate the effectiveness of our Seaf in achieving effective and scalable comprehension of long-form videos.

papers.title: ScaleGS: Towards Scalable and Efficient 3d Gaussian Splatting
alternate_titles: ScaleGS: Towards Scalable and Efficient 3d Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has recently gained attention as an efficient neural rendering approach, supporting real-time reconstruction, virtual reality, and large-scale scene reconstruction. However, multi-GPU training of 3DGS still faces challenges such as redundant gradient updates across views and inefficient GPU utilization, leading to slow convergence. To address these issues, we introduce ScaleGS, an efficient multi-GPU training framework for 3DGS. ScaleGS incorporates three mechanisms: (1) a Multi-View Visibility-Gated Update that prunes Gaussian updates irrelevant to each camera view; (2) a Masked Fused-SSIM loss that accelerates convergence by incorporating perceptual similarity into the reconstruction objective; and (3) a Batch Update Strategy that decouples Gaussian and spherical harmonics parameter updates. We evaluate ScaleGS on MipNeRF, DeepBlending, and Tanks & Temples,...

papers.title: Robust MAE-Driven NAS: From Mask Reconstruction to Architecture Innovation
alternate_titles: Robust MAE-Driven NAS: From Mask Reconstruction to Architecture Innovation
papers.abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) relies heavily on labeled data, which is labor-intensive and time-consuming to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel NAS method based on an unsupervised paradigm, specifically Masked Autoencoders (MAE), thereby eliminating the need for labeled data. By replacing the supervised learning objective with an image reconstruction task, our approach enables the efficient discovery of network architectures without compromising performance and generalization ability. Additionally, we address the problem of performance collapse encountered in the widely-used Differentiable Architecture Search (DARTS) in the unsupervised setting by designing a hierarchical decoder. Extensive experiments across various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our method, offering empirical evidence of its superiority over the counterparts.

papers.title: ReflectMT: Internalizing Reflection for Efficient and High-Quality Machine Translation
alternate_titles: ReflectMT: Internalizing Reflection for Efficient and High-Quality Machine Translation
papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed growing interest in applying Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) to Machine Translation (MT). Existing approaches predominantly adopt a "think-first-then-translate" paradigm. Although explicit reasoning trajectories significantly enhance translation quality, they incur prohibitive inference costs and latency. To address these limitations, we propose ReflectMT, a two-stage reflection internalization algorithm for machine translation that employs a "translate-first-think-later" paradigm. Our approach develops the model's "translate-reflect-refine" capability through reinforcement learning. In the first stage, we cultivate the model's capacity for high-quality reflection and refinement, thereby enhancing its semantic comprehension and task-specific knowledge. In the second stage, we train the model to internalize the knowledge acquired during reflection. As a result, d...

papers.title: Ranking-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Ordinal Ranking
alternate_titles: Ranking-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Ordinal Ranking
papers.abstract: Ordinal regression and ranking are challenging due to inherent ordinal dependencies that conventional methods struggle to model. We propose Ranking-Aware Reinforcement Learning (RARL), a novel RL framework that explicitly learns these relationships. At its core, RARL features a unified objective that synergistically integrates regression and Learning-to-Rank (L2R), enabling mutual improvement between the two tasks. This is driven by a ranking-aware verifiable reward that jointly assesses regression precision and ranking accuracy, facilitating direct model updates via policy optimization. To further enhance training, we introduce Response Mutation Operations (RMO), which inject controlled noise to improve exploration and prevent stagnation at saddle points. The effectiveness of RARL is validated through extensive experiments on three distinct benchmarks.

papers.title: RLBR: Reinforcement Learning with Biasing Rewards for Contextual Speech Large Language Models
alternate_titles: RLBR: Reinforcement Learning with Biasing Rewards for Contextual Speech Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Speech large language models (LLMs) have driven significant progress in end-to-end speech understanding and recognition, yet they continue to struggle with accurately recognizing rare words and domain-specific terminology. This paper presents a novel fine-tuning method, Reinforcement Learning with Biasing Rewards (RLBR), which employs a specialized biasing words preferred reward to explicitly emphasize biasing words in the reward calculation. In addition, we introduce reference-aware mechanisms that extend the reinforcement learning algorithm with reference transcription to strengthen the potential trajectory exploration space. Experiments on the LibriSpeech corpus across various biasing list sizes demonstrate that RLBR delivers substantial performance improvements over strong supervised fine-tuning (SFT) baseline and consistently outperforms several recently published methods. papers.title: Production-Scale Dynamic Vocabulary ASR Biasing with Word-Level FST and Robust Training
alternate_titles: Production-Scale Dynamic Vocabulary ASR Biasing with Word-Level FST and Robust Training
papers.abstract: Contextual biasing is a critical component in enhancing Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) performance, particularly for domain-specific or rare entities. Recent advances introduce a dynamic vocabulary (DynVoc) method that augments the output dictionary with full bias phrases, enabling phrase-level decoding in a single step and providing an elegant and simple solution with good recall.Despite the advantages of the DynVoc approach, there are several challenges associated with it for production-scale deployment. First, the original DynVoc approach struggles with overlapping or multi-word phrases, often causing repetition errors and recognition degradation. Second, DynVoc tends to overbias and produce high false-alarm rates, which might not be suitable from customer perspective due to the less reliable output entities. Third, the general ASR accuracy degrades relative to a vanilla ASR syste...

papers.title: Predicting Heart Failure Outcomes Using Machine Learning Models on Clinical and Laboratory Data
alternate_titles: Predicting Heart Failure Outcomes Using Machine Learning Models on Clinical and Laboratory Data
papers.abstract: Heart failure is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, requiring timely and accurate prediction to guide clinical decision-making. This study explores the use of machine learning models to predict mortality outcomes in patients with heart failure using clinical and laboratory data from 296 individuals. The dataset was obtained from the UCI Machine Learning Repository and includes variables such as age, comorbidities, vital signs, and laboratory test results.Four models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation: logistic regression, decision tree, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Among these, logistic regression achieved the highest overall accuracy (0.74) and precision (0.64), while XGBoost demonstrated strong recall for identifying high-risk patients, highlighting its ability to capture complex, non-linear relationships in clinical data. papers.title: Poly-SVC: Polyphony-Aware Singing Voice Conversion with Harmonic Modeling
alternate_titles: Poly-SVC: Polyphony-Aware Singing Voice Conversion with Harmonic Modeling
papers.abstract: Singing Voice Conversion (SVC) aims to transform a source singing voice into a target singer while preserving lyrics and melody. Most existing SVC methods depend on F0 extractors to capture the lead melody from clean vocals. However, no existing method can reliably extract clean vocals from accompanied recordings without leaving residual harmonies behind. In this paper, we innovatively propose Poly-SVC, a zero-shot, cross-lingual singing voice conversion system designed to process residual harmonies. Poly-SVC is composed of three key components: a Constant-Q Transform (CQT)-based pitch extractor to preserve both the lead melody and residual harmony, a random sampler to reduce interference information from the CQT and a diffusion decoder based on Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) that fuses pitch, content, and timbre features into natural-sounding polyphonic outputs. papers.title: One-Step Generative Distillation
alternate_titles: One-Step Generative Distillation
papers.abstract: We present MeanFlow Distillation (MF-KD), a novel knowledge distillation framework that overcomes key limitations of diffusion-based distillation methods by enabling efficient one-step generative modeling. While recent approaches such as DiffKD treat student features as noisy inputs to a denoising process, they incur significant computational costs due to multi-step sampling (typically 50–100 steps), suffer from irreversible information loss caused by Gaussian noise corruption, and are prone to errors from discrete timestep approximations. In contrast, MF-KD introduces the concept of average velocity fields, characterized by the MeanFlow Identity, which allows direct and lossless transformation between teacher and student representations in a single step. papers.title: On deepfake voice detection - It’s all in the presentation
alternate_titles: On deepfake voice detection - It’s all in the presentation
papers.abstract: While the technologies empowering malicious audio deepfakes have dramatically evolved in recent years due to generative AI advances, the same cannot be said of global research into spoofing (deepfake) countermeasures. This paper highlights how current deepfake datasets and research methodologies led to systems that failed to generalize to real world application. The main reason is due to the difference between raw deepfake audio, and deepfake audio that has been presented through a communication channel, e.g. by phone. We propose a new framework for data creation and research methodology, allowing for the development of spoofing countermeasures that would be more effective in real-world scenarios. By following the guidelines outlined here we improved deepfake detection accuracy by 39% in more robust and realistic lab setups, and by 57% on a real-world benchmark. We also demonstrate how i...

papers.title: O-Band 8x8x8λ Wavelength Selective Optical Cross-Connect Switch for Data Center Networks
alternate_titles: O-Band 8x8x8λ Wavelength Selective Optical Cross-Connect Switch for Data Center Networks
papers.abstract: Driven by the rapid expansion of AI and cloud-based workloads, intra-data center connections demand scalable, flexible, and energy-efficient all-optical switching technologies. Considering the diverse internal traffic patterns in data centers, wavelength-selective optical cross-connect (WSOXC) switch enables flexible reconfiguration in wavelength, space, time, bandwidth, and routing, providing an efficient solution for dynamic traffic adaptation. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate a fast (sub-microseconds) low loss and crosstalk and polarization independent 8 channels O-band 4×4×8λ and 8×8×8λ WSOXC switch. The modular WSOXC switch is based on ultra-low crosstalk, flat-top and polarization independent AWGs and SOAs wavelength switches with 400 GHz wavelength spacing. The proposed WSOXC exhibits low loss both for the 4×4 and 8×8 configurations, with crosstalk below –40 dB. In 800....

papers.title: NanoCodec: Towards Low Bitrate and Low Complexity Real-Time Neural Audio Codec
alternate_titles: NanoCodec: Towards Low Bitrate and Low Complexity Real-Time Neural Audio Codec
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present NanoCodec, our submitted system for the LRAC Challenge, which can effectively reconstruct target waveform under ultra-low and low bitrate conditions. Specifically, our architecture operates in the time-frequency (T-F) domain, where we encode the magnitude feature in the encoder side, and both magnitude and phase are estimated at the receiver side. In addition, we propose an efficient convolutional-style attention block as the core modeling unit. For magnitude and phase reconstruction, the omnidirectional phase and real-imaginary losses are introduced to enable the effective joint optimization of target magnitude and phase components. Under the given restrictions on computational complexity and processing delay, our submitted system achieved second place in Track 1 and third place in Track 2.

papers.title: Multi-Scale Task-Aware EEG Representation Learning for Cognitive State Recognition
alternate_titles: Multi-Scale Task-Aware EEG Representation Learning for Cognitive State Recognition
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has become an important tool for cognitive state assessment. Although deep learning methods have achieved remarkable progress in this area, most existing approaches overlook the heterogeneous encoding patterns across different brain regions and the multi-scale dynamics of neural activity, which limits the reliability and generalization of EEG representations. To address this issue, we propose MSTA-EEGNet, a multi-scale task-aware network for EEG-based cognitive state recognition. In this framework, EEG channels are partitioned into multiple functional regions, with independent encoders assigned to each region to capture distinct neural patterns. A multi-scale feature extraction strategy is further introduced to model neural dynamics across different time resolutions. papers.title: Multi-Domain Audio Question Answering Benchmark toward Acoustic Content Reasoning
alternate_titles: Multi-Domain Audio Question Answering Benchmark toward Acoustic Content Reasoning
papers.abstract: We introduce a multi-domain Audio Question Answering (MD-Audio) benchmark designed to advance research in multi-domain sound understanding. The task is organized into three subsets (Bioacoustics, Temporal Soundscapes, and Complex QA), each targeting distinct aspects of interactive question answering over diverse acoustic environments. The benchmark encompasses a broad range of auditory material, including marine mammal vocalizations, environmental soundscapes, and complex real-world audio recordings. We further detail the evaluation protocol, which employs top-1 accuracy alongside an answer-shuffling robustness criterion, and provide baseline results using state-of-the-art audio-language models (Qwen2-Audio-7B, AudioFlamingo 2, and Gemini-2-Flash). papers.title: Multi Stage Training with Dynamic Data Balancing for Multilingual Speech Recognition and Translation
alternate_titles: Multi Stage Training with Dynamic Data Balancing for Multilingual Speech Recognition and Translation
papers.abstract: Training large-scale multilingual speech models is often hindered by severe data imbalances across tasks, languages, and corpora. We introduce a systematic, multi-stage training framework to ad-dress this challenge. First, for pre-training on 1.7 million hours of speech across 25 languages, we propose an inverted two-tier sampling policy that prioritizes balancing corpora within each language before balancing across languages, enhancing data diversity. Second, during fine-tuning, we apply a dynamic data balancing schedule that smoothly transitions the data mixture from the initial imbalanced state to a targeted, high-quality distribution using a co-sine schedule. This gradual adaptation prevents catastrophic forget-ting and maximizes performance. Our resulting 1-billion parameter model, Canary-1B-v2, demonstrates the success of this methodology, achieving state-of-the-art multilingual AS...

papers.title: More Than a Shortcut: A Hyperbolic Approach to Early-Exit Networks
alternate_titles: More Than a Shortcut: A Hyperbolic Approach to Early-Exit Networks
papers.abstract: Deploying accurate event detection on resource-constrained devices is challenged by the trade-off between performance and computational cost. While Early-Exit (EE) networks offer a solution through adaptive computation, they often fail to enforce a coherent hierarchical structure, limiting the reliability of their early predictions. To address this, we propose Hyperbolic Early-Exit networks (HypEE), a novel framework that learns EE representations in the hyperbolic space. Our core contribution is a hierarchical training objective with a novel entailment loss, which enforces a partial-ordering constraint to ensure that deeper network layers geometrically refine the representations of shallower ones. papers.title: Mongoose: do we Need a Scanner for Vision Mamba?
alternate_titles: Mongoose: do we Need a Scanner for Vision Mamba?
papers.abstract: Self-attention, the backbone of transformers, faces challenges with quadratic complexity in long-context sequences, affecting training and inference throughput. State Space Models (SSMs) are an alternative architecture to address this issue. Mamba and its variants (Vim, VMamba, SiMBA) are well-known SSMs for vision tasks. However, these existing methods introduce computational overhead due to specialized scanning techniques. To address these issues, we propose Mongoose, a simplified SSM that eliminates scanning mechanisms. Mongoose reduces complexity, training significantly faster 1.5X faster than other SSMs (Vim, VMamba, and SiMBA) on V100 GPUs. It achieves state-of-the-art SSM results on the ImageNet dataset, reaching 85.7% accuracy on a large network size, matching top transformers. papers.title: MoEvalSong: A Mixture-of-Experts Model for Automatic Song Aesthetics Evaluation
alternate_titles: MoEvalSong: A Mixture-of-Experts Model for Automatic Song Aesthetics Evaluation
papers.abstract: Aesthetic evaluation is essential for judging the quality of generated music, yet it remains largely underexplored. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model, naming MoEvalSong for song evaluation. The MoE gating network integrates multi-faceted and multi-level musical aesthetic features derived from various feature extractors,including MuQ, music2latent, MERT, UTMOS, Qwen3-Omni-captioner, and LeVo. Weights are adaptively assigned to each fine-grained feature, thereby enhancing evaluation accuracy. MoEvalSong is evaluated in the Automatic Song Aesthetics Evaluation Challenge - ICASSP 2026. It achieves a score of 0.655 on the final fine-grained aesthetic prediction test set, claiming the 1st place in the Fine-grained Dimension Prediction (track 2) of the challenge.

papers.title: MixGAN-based Non-blind Bandwidth Extension for Audio Codec
alternate_titles: MixGAN-based Non-blind Bandwidth Extension for Audio Codec
papers.abstract: Bandwidth extension (BWE) enhances audio quality by reconstructing high-frequency (HF) band from the low-frequency (LF) band. Despite the proliferation of AI-based BWE methods, a solution designed for integration into audio codecs remains unexplored. To bridge this gap, we propose the MixGAN-based BWE scheme that addresses practical codec constraints including quantization, delay, and decoding distortion. The integrated MixGAN framework stabilizes adversarial training and improves reconstruction fidelity. This work presents the first AI-based non-blind BWE method that extracts a few bits of side information from the encoder to guide HF reconstruction. papers.title: Mitigating Deceptive Knowledge Editing in LLMS via Diffusion Synthesis
alternate_titles: Mitigating Deceptive Knowledge Editing in LLMS via Diffusion Synthesis
papers.abstract: The reliability of large language models depends on their ability to incorporate new knowledge. However, current editing methods introduce a hidden vulnerability: models that seem to be successfully updated, but deceptively revert to their original outputs with even slight variations in prompts. We propose DiffEdit, a novel diffusion-based framework that transforms abrupt parameter changes into stable, smooth transitions through iterative refinement. DiffEdit first identifies relevant knowledge subspaces and then applies controlled diffusion processes to generate stable edit layers. Extensive experiments on CounterFact and ZsRE datasets demonstrate 98.6% editing efficacy, with improvements in generalization and fluency by 4.6% and 9.6% respectively compared to state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Micro Language Models Enable Instant Responses
alternate_titles: Micro Language Models Enable Instant Responses
papers.abstract: Edge devices such as smartwatches and smart glasses cannot continuously run even the smallest 100M-1B parameter language models due to power and compute constraints, yet cloud inference introduces multi-second latencies that break the illusion of a responsive assistant. We introduce micro language models ($μ$LMs): ultra-compact models (8M-30M parameters) that instantly generate the first 4-8 words of a contextually grounded response on-device, while a cloud model completes it; thus, masking the cloud latency. We show that useful language generation survives at this extreme scale with our models matching several 70M-256M-class existing models. We design a collaborative generation framework that reframes the cloud model as a continuator rather than a respondent, achieving seamless mid-sentence handoffs and structured graceful recovery via three error correction methods when the local opene...

papers.title: Measuring Prosody Diversity in Zero-Shot TTS: A New Metric, Benchmark, and Exploration
alternate_titles: Measuring Prosody Diversity in Zero-Shot TTS: A New Metric, Benchmark, and Exploration
papers.abstract: Prosody diversity is essential for achieving naturalness and expressiveness in zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS). However, frequently used acoustic metrics capture only partial views of prosodic variation and correlate poorly with human perception, leaving the problem of reliably quantifying prosody diversity underexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce ProsodyEval, a prosody diversity assessment dataset that provides Prosody Mean Opinion Score (PMOS) along-side conventional acoustic metrics. ProsodyEval comprises 1000 speech samples derived from 7 mainstream TTS systems, with 2000 human ratings. Building on this, we propose the Discretized Speech Weighted Edit Distance (DS-WED), a new objective diversity metric that quantifies prosodic variation via weighted edit distance over semantic tokens. Experiments on ProsodyEval show that DS-WED achieves substantially higher correlation with hum...

papers.title: Mambaformer: State-Space Augmented Self-Attention with Downup Sampling for Monaural Speech Enhancement
alternate_titles: Mambaformer: State-Space Augmented Self-Attention with Downup Sampling for Monaural Speech Enhancement
papers.abstract: While Transformers excel at global context modeling and state-space models (SSMs) provide efficient sequential processing, prior speech enhancement methods have not effectively combined these complementary strengths. We present MambaFormer, which unifies SSMs and Transformers within a dual-path time–frequency framework to improve monaural speech enhancement. Specifically, our model fuses Mamba’s adaptive state-space modeling into Transformer self-attention to achieve simultaneous local refinement and long-range dependency capture, and we further incorporate Conformer-style convolutions to preserve spectral continuity. For efficiency, we use weight sharing in self-attentions and process features at multiple resolutions via symmetric down/up-sampling stacks. Moreover, dual decoders are adopted to explicitly reconstruct magnitude and phase. This integrated design combining adaptive state-sp...

papers.title: MTAD: A Three-Stage Framework for Machine Translation Agents Distillation
alternate_titles: MTAD: A Three-Stage Framework for Machine Translation Agents Distillation
papers.abstract: Despite recent progress, translation agents often face inefficiency and limited accuracy in domain-specific tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a Translation Agent Distillation Framework that integrates supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), and group relative policy optimization (GRPO). In the first stage, we tune a translation agent with SFT using agent-generated translations, and further refine it with DPO. The DPO data come from two complementary sources: (1) translation-agent self-improvement, where initial outputs are revised through a pipeline of initial translation → LQA feedback → improved translation; and (2) style-guided post-editing, where bad cases are aligned with human-calibrated corrections under explicit style guides. In the second stage, we train an AILQA agent to assess translation quality. Two GRPO strategies are then considered...

papers.title: MELA-TTS: Joint Transformer-Diffusion Model with Representation Alignment for Speech Synthesis
alternate_titles: MELA-TTS: Joint Transformer-Diffusion Model with Representation Alignment for Speech Synthesis
papers.abstract: This work introduces MELA-TTS, a novel joint transformer-diffusion framework for end-to-end text-to-speech synthesis. By autoregressively generating continuous mel-spectrogram frames from linguistic and speaker conditions, our architecture eliminates the need for speech tokenization and multi-stage processing pipelines. To address the inherent difficulties of modeling continuous features, we propose a representation alignment module that aligns output representations of the transformer decoder with semantic embeddings from a pretrained ASR encoder during training. This mechanism not only speeds up training convergence, but also enhances cross-modal coherence between the textual and acoustic domains. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that MELA-TTS achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple evaluation metrics while maintaining robust zero-shot voice cloning capabilities, in....

papers.title: MECap-R1: Emotion-Aware Policy with Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Emotion Captioning
alternate_titles: MECap-R1: Emotion-Aware Policy with Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Emotion Captioning
papers.abstract: Speech Emotion Captioning (SEC) has emerged as a notable research direction. The inherent complexity of emotional content in human speech makes it challenging for traditional discrete classification methods to provide an adequate representation. Consequently, utilizing natural language to describe speech emotions presents a novel avenue for more effectively capturing and expressing affect. In this paper, we propose MECap-R1, a pioneering emotion-aware policy with reinforcement learning for multimodal emotion captioning. By employing Group Relative Policy Optimization with emotion-aware reward (Emo-GRPO), the framework precisely captures the emotion and semantic features, thereby addressing the shortcomings of rigid rules in handling the dynamic and flexible nature of captions. Experimental results on the EmotionTalk dataset demonstrate that MECap-R1 performs well in generating emotion de...

papers.title: MC-MRX: Reference- and Midi-Guided Music Source Extraction with Contrastive Learning
alternate_titles: MC-MRX: Reference- and Midi-Guided Music Source Extraction with Contrastive Learning
papers.abstract: Music Source Extraction (MSE) is a foundational task for symphonic education and re-creation. However, existing approaches face two primary limitations: source feature confusion and timbre mismatch bias, which arise from their inadequate modeling of the inherent properties of musical signals. We argue that these challenges can be fundamentally addressed by effectively leveraging multimodal cues. To this end, we propose a novel framework that integrates Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) temporal pitch anchors and reference audio within a contrastive learning paradigm. Our design generates monophonic MIDI from the mixed audio, providing structured, content-aware guidance for the extraction process. Additionally, we employ joint optimization of Contrastive Loss (CL) and Scale Invariant Signal-to-Noise Ratio loss (SI-SNR) to enhance target track focusing and fidelity. Our method si...

papers.title: LoopCTR: Unlocking the Loop Scaling Power for Click-Through Rate Prediction
alternate_titles: LoopCTR: Unlocking the Loop Scaling Power for Click-Through Rate Prediction
papers.abstract: Scaling Transformer-based click-through rate (CTR) models by stacking more parameters brings growing computational and storage overhead, creating a widening gap between scaling ambitions and the stringent industrial deployment constraints. We propose LoopCTR, which introduces a loop scaling paradigm that increases training-time computation through recursive reuse of shared model layers, decoupling computation from parameter growth. LoopCTR adopts a sandwich architecture enhanced with Hyper-Connected Residuals and Mixture-of-Experts, and employs process supervision at every loop depth to encode multi-loop benefits into the shared parameters. This enables a train-multi-loop, infer-zero-loop strategy where a single forward pass without any loop already outperforms all baselines. Experiments on three public benchmarks and one industrial dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. Oracl...

papers.title: Legal∆: Enhancing Legal Reasoning in LLMS via Reinforcement Learning with Chain-Of-Thought Guided Information Gain
alternate_titles: Legal∆: Enhancing Legal Reasoning in LLMS via Reinforcement Learning with Chain-Of-Thought Guided Information Gain
papers.abstract: Legal Artificial Intelligence (LegalAI) has achieved notable advances in automating judicial decision-making with the support of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, existing legal LLMs still struggle to generate reliable and interpretable reasoning processes. They often default to fast-thinking behavior by producing direct answers without explicit multi-step reasoning, limiting their effectiveness in complex legal scenarios that demand rigorous justification. To address this challenge, we propose Legal∆, a reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance legal reasoning through chain-of-thought guided information gain. During training, Legal∆ employs a dual-mode input setup—comprising direct answer and reasoning-augmented modes—and maximizes the information gain between them. This encourages the model to acquire meaningful reasoning patterns rather than generating superficial or r...

papers.title: Lattice-Guided Consistency Regularization of Dual-Mode Transducers for Automatic Speech Recognition
alternate_titles: Lattice-Guided Consistency Regularization of Dual-Mode Transducers for Automatic Speech Recognition
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel approach to train a dual-mode transducer model that supports both autoregressive (AR) and non-autoregressive (NAR) inference using lattice-based consistency regularization for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). Our model is trained with a loss function that incorporates both AR and NAR objectives, plus a regularization term that minimizes the difference between AR and NAR procedures, weighted by lattice posteriors. Experiments on monolingual ASR tasks achieve a relative improvement 6.42% on the test set of AISHELL-1 compared to AR Hybrid-Autoregressive Inference Transducer (HAINAN) baseline. Evaluations on the SEAME Mandarin-English Code-switching dataset show relative Mixed Error Rate reductions of 7.76% on test_man and 7.09% on test_sge sets. When inference in NAR mode, proposed model can achieve superior performances compared to other AR models including RNN Tran...

papers.title: LOGIX: Local-Global Mixers for Time Series Representation Learning
alternate_titles: LOGIX: Local-Global Mixers for Time Series Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Time series analysis faces challenges such as capturing long-term and short-term dependencies, handling diverse data sources, ensuring efficiency, and resisting noise. Transformer-based models excel at modeling long-range dependencies, but often struggle with computational cost, time-domain modeling, and explicit temporal transformations. This paper proposes LoGix, a new architecture for time series representation that combines local and global frequency mixers to capture both detailed and broad patterns using unique frequency mixing strategies. The local mixer operates in the time domain with different convolutional kernels, while the global mixer works in the frequency domain using multiple filter sets. Our experiments demonstrate that LoGix outperforms the state-of-the-art models in various time series tasks, highlighting its robustness and scalability across different noise levels an...

papers.title: LLMPopcorn: Exploring LLMS as Assistants for Popular Micro-Video Generation
alternate_titles: LLMPopcorn: Exploring LLMS as Assistants for Popular Micro-Video Generation
papers.abstract: In an era where micro-videos dominate platforms like TikTok and YouTube, AI-generated content is nearing cinematic quality. The next frontier is using large language models (LLMs) to autonomously create viral micro-videos, a largely untapped potential that could shape the future of AI-driven content creation. To address this gap, this paper presents the first exploration of LLM-assisted popular micro-video generation (LLMPopcorn1). Specifically, we empirically study the following research questions: (i) How can LLMs be effectively utilized to assist popular micro-video generation? (ii) To what extent can prompt-based enhancements optimize the LLM-generated content for higher popularity? (iii) How well do various LLMs and video generators perform in the popular micro-video generation task? Exploring these questions, we show that advanced LLMs like DeepSeek-V3 can generate micro-videos wit...

papers.title: Joint Single-Shot ToA and DoA Estimation for VAA-Based BLE Ranging with Phase Ambiguity: A Deep Learning-Based Approach
alternate_titles: Joint Single-Shot ToA and DoA Estimation for VAA-Based BLE Ranging with Phase Ambiguity: A Deep Learning-Based Approach
papers.abstract: Conventional direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation methods rely on multi-antenna arrays, which are costly to implement on size-constrained Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) devices. Virtual antenna array (VAA) techniques enable DoA estimation with a single antenna, making angle estimation feasible on such devices. However, BLE only provides a single-shot two-way channel frequency response (CFR) with a binary phase ambiguity issue, which hinders the direct application of VAA. To address this challenge, we propose a unified model that combines VAA with BLE two-way CFR, and introduce a neural network–based phase recovery framework that employs row/column predictors with a voting mechanism to resolve the ambiguity. The recovered one-way CFR then enables super-resolution algorithms such as MUSIC for joint time-of-arrival (ToA) and DoA estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed meth...

papers.title: Joint Multichannel Acoustic Feedback Cancellation and Speaker Extraction via Kalman Filter and Deep Non-Linear Spatial Filter
alternate_titles: Joint Multichannel Acoustic Feedback Cancellation and Speaker Extraction via Kalman Filter and Deep Non-Linear Spatial Filter
papers.abstract: Acoustic feedback cancellation (AFC) and speech enhancement are essential techniques in audio systems, and several conventional multichannel signal processing approaches have been developed to combine them. In this work, a data-driven microphone array algorithm, termed AFC-SPEX, is proposed. It integrates a deep non-linear spatial filter (DNSF) with an adaptive feedback cancellation module to enable target speech extraction in the presence of both acoustic feedback and interference, without reliance on prior knowledge of the interfering source direction. The AFC module is implemented using a partitioned block frequency-domain Kalman filter to ensure low latency and fast convergence. The DNSF is trained offline using a teacher-forced strategy, where an open-loop dataset is constructed to accelerate training. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed AFC-SPEX consistently outperforms a rec...

papers.title: Int-MeanFlow: Few-Step Speech Generation with Integral Velocity Distillation
alternate_titles: Int-MeanFlow: Few-Step Speech Generation with Integral Velocity Distillation
papers.abstract: Flow-based generative models have greatly improved text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis quality, but inference speed remains limited by the iterative sampling process and multiple function evaluations (NFE). The recent MeanFlow model accelerates generation by modeling average velocity instead of instantaneous velocity. However, its direct application to TTS encounters challenges, including GPU memory overhead from Jacobian-vector products (JVP) and training instability due to self-bootstrap processes. To address these issues, we introduce IntMeanFlow, a framework for few-step speech generation with integral velocity distillation. By approximating average velocity with the teacher’s instantaneous velocity over a temporal interval, IntMeanFlow eliminates the need for JVPs and self-bootstrap, improving stability and reducing GPU memory usage. We also propose the Optimal Step Sampling Search (OS3)...

papers.title: Input-Adaptive Differentiable Filterbanks via Hypernetworks for Robust Speech Processing
alternate_titles: Input-Adaptive Differentiable Filterbanks via Hypernetworks for Robust Speech Processing
papers.abstract: Traditional audio front-ends rely on static filters that fail in diverse acoustic environments. We propose HyperFB, a novel front-end that fundamentally overcomes this limitation by adapting its physical filter parameters in real-time. Our core innovation is a lightweight Hypernetwork that analyzes the input signal’s acoustic context to generate a continuous trajectory of optimal filter configurations (e.g., center frequencies, bandwidths). This elevates the front-end to an intelligent, self-regulating system. Through a task-agnostic self-supervised pre-training strategy [1], [2], HyperFB learns a robust and general-purpose representation. Experiments on challenging noisy speech recognition (CHiME-4), emotion recognition, and audio classification benchmarks show that our adaptive approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art static and large pre-trained baselines.

papers.title: ISSE: An Instruction-Guided Speech Style Editing Dataset and Benchmark
alternate_titles: ISSE: An Instruction-Guided Speech Style Editing Dataset and Benchmark
papers.abstract: Speech style editing refers to modifying the stylistic properties of speech while preserving its linguistic content and speaker identity. However, most existing approaches depend on explicit labels or reference audio, which limits both flexibility and scalability. More recent attempts to use natural language descriptions remain constrained by oversimplified instructions and coarse style control. To address these limitations, we introduce an Instruction-guided Speech Style Editing Dataset (ISSE). The dataset comprises nearly 400 hours of speech and over 100,000 source-target pairs, each aligned with diverse and detailed textual editing instructions. We also build a systematic instructed speech data generation pipeline leveraging large language model, expressive text-to-speech and voice conversion technologies to construct high-quality paired samples. Furthermore, we train an instruction-g...

papers.title: IRIS: Low-Complexity High-Efficiency Neural Network Codec for Real-Time Audio Transmission
alternate_titles: IRIS: Low-Complexity High-Efficiency Neural Network Codec for Real-Time Audio Transmission
papers.abstract: The 2025 Low-Resource Audio Codec (LRAC) Challenge aims to advance the development of low-resource neural audio codec. It requires participating systems to achieve high-quality audio compression under strict resource constraints. LRAC Challenge Track 1 focuses on transparent audio transmission under real-world noise and reverberation, while Track 2 integrates speech enhancement and transmission. This paper introduces IRIS (Internet Real-time Intelligent Streaming Codec): an end-to-end, low-complexity, low-latency neural audio codec. IRIS enables encoding and decoding at bitrates of 1 kbps and 6 kbps, with inherent robustness to noise and reverberation. We designed a lightweight codec architecture, incorporating multiple discriminators and loss functions to achieve high-quality reconstruction at extremely low complexity and bitrates. In the LRAC Challenge, IRIS ranked first in Track 1, de...

papers.title: How Does Instrumental Music Help Singfake Detection?
alternate_titles: How Does Instrumental Music Help Singfake Detection?
papers.abstract: Although many models exist to detect singing voice deepfakes (SingFake), how these models operate, particularly with instrumental accompaniment, is unclear. We investigate how instrumental music affects SingFake detection from two perspectives. To investigate the behavioral effect, we test different backbones, unpaired instrumental tracks, and frequency subbands. To analyze the representational effect, we probe how fine-tuning alters encoders’ speech and music capabilities. Our results show that instrumental accompaniment acts mainly as data augmentation rather than providing intrinsic cues (e.g., rhythm or harmony). Furthermore, fine-tuning increases reliance on shallow speaker features while reducing sensitivity to content, paralinguistic, and semantic information. These insights clarify how models exploit vocal versus instrumental cues and can inform the design of more interpretable a...

papers.title: High Quality Underwater Image Compression with Adaptive Color Correction
alternate_titles: High Quality Underwater Image Compression with Adaptive Color Correction
papers.abstract: With the increasing exploration and exploitation of the underwater world, underwater images have become a critical medium for human interaction with marine environments, driving extensive research into their efficient transmission and storage. However, contemporary underwater image compression algorithms fail to adequately address the impact of water refraction and scattering on light waves, which not only elevate training complexity but also result in suboptimal compression performance. To tackle this limitation, we propose High Quality Underwater Image Compression (HQUIC), a novel framework designed to handle the unique illumination conditions and color shifts inherent in underwater images, thereby achieving superior compression performance. HQUIC first incorporates an Adaptive Lighting and Tone Correction (ALTC) module to adaptively predict the attenuation coefficients and global ligh...

papers.title: Harnessing the Gradient: Enhanced Cross-Prompt Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models
alternate_titles: Harnessing the Gradient: Enhanced Cross-Prompt Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent large vision–language models (LVLMs) have attracted increasing attention for their strong performance on multi-modal understanding tasks conditioned on textual instructions. However, they remain vulnerable to adversarial examples where imperceptible image perturbations can induce harmful or targeted outputs, posing deployment risks. Unlike single-modal models, LVLMs process both image and text simultaneously, making the creation of visual adversarial examples dependent on specific prompts. Consequently, adversarial examples often fail to transfer across prompts. To address this challenge, we propose the Gradient Regularization-based Cross-Prompt Attack (GrCPA), a general framework that employs gradient regularization to generate more robust and transferable adversarial examples. GrCPA reduces the variance of back-propagated gradients within Transformer Attention and MLP components...

papers.title: HarmoNet: Music Grounding by Short Video via Harmonic Resample and Dynamic Sparse Alignment
alternate_titles: HarmoNet: Music Grounding by Short Video via Harmonic Resample and Dynamic Sparse Alignment
papers.abstract: Automatically selecting the appropriate background music by short videos, named MGSV(Music Grounding for Short Videos), is a crucial step in content creation. Although current studies have established benchmarks and models, they ignore modeling the different melodic scales between videos and music and dynamic changes in sequence importance caused by tempo variations. To address these issues, we propose HarmoNet. Firstly, we design the HRM (Harmonic Resample Module), which resample the music signal across multiple time scales into different perspectives of music dimensions and then rematch it with the video representation. Secondly, we develop the DSA (Dynamic Sparse Alignment) strategy to selectively focus on modality cues in different rhythm sequences, achieving better localization of the music segment. Comprehensive experiments show that HarmoNet is state-of-the-art.

papers.title: Hadamard Tensor Ring for Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning
alternate_titles: Hadamard Tensor Ring for Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: We propose Hadamard Tensor Ring (HTR), a novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that leverages tensor ring decomposition with Hadamard product operations for large-scale pre-trained models. Our approach addresses the limitations of existing low-rank adaptation methods by introducing a cyclic tensor structure that enables more expressive parameter updates while maintaining computational efficiency. We formulate the weight update matrices as tensor rings with learnable factors, incorporating Hadamard products to capture element-wise interactions between different rank components. Through alternating minimization and efficient initialization strategies inspired by tensor completion theory, we achieve superior parameter efficiency compared to existing methods. papers.title: HLF: A Hierarchical Localization Framework for Joint Moment Retrieval and Highlight Detection
alternate_titles: HLF: A Hierarchical Localization Framework for Joint Moment Retrieval and Highlight Detection
papers.abstract: Video Moment Retrieval (MR) and Highlight Detection (HD) are closely related tasks that involve localizing semantically relevant video segments in untrimmed videos using natural language queries. Existing approaches struggle with the challenge of scattered relevant segments and varying durations, thereby resulting in limited localization performance. In this paper, we propose a Hierarchical Localization Framework (HLF) leveraging semantic relevance identification and hierarchical temporal perception to address both MR and HD tasks jointly. Specifically, we design a Video Feature Orientation (VFO) mechanism that explicitly computes token-level semantic importance by jointly considering attention distributions and cross-modal similarity cues. Subsequently, we employ a hierarchical information perception module designed to effectively capture diverse temporal patterns and leverage multi-sca...

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Reconstruction of Large Vision-Language Models from Dense into Mixture-of-Experts
alternate_titles: Geometry-Aware Reconstruction of Large Vision-Language Models from Dense into Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at cross-modal reasoning but incur high computational costs due to dense parameter activation. Recent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures reduce this burden through sparsification. However, existing methods struggle to reconcile expert specialization with cross-modal collaboration, leading to degraded performance. We propose DMoE, a geometry-aware reconstruction framework that addresses this tradeoff by migrating computations to hyperbolic space. This enables expert collaboration while maintaining specialization through adaptive allocation and consistency constraints. DMoE transforms dense VLMs into sparse architectures while preserving cross-modal understanding. Experiments show that DMoE outperforms MoE-LLaVA by up to 5.8% on VQAv2 under similar 3B activation budgets.

alternate_titles: Gala: Dual Alignments for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation with Limited Source Labels
papers.abstract: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) improves generalization by aligning feature distributions but typically requires abundant labeled source data, which is often impractical. Few-shot Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (FS-UDA) mitigates this by leveraging only a few labeled source samples, yet label scarcity still restricts domain-invariant learning. To address this, we propose Fusion of Global Adversarial Alignment and Local Category Prototype Alignment (GALA), a novel FS-UDA framework. GALA expands the effective source set through selective sampling and introduces a prototype alignment loss weighted by prediction probabilities, without relying on additional unlabeled source data. By integrating prototype-based local alignment with adversarial global alignment, GALA achieves more comprehensive adaptation. papers.title: GUI-ARP: Enhancing Grounding with Adaptive Region Perception for GUI Agents
alternate_titles: GUI-ARP: Enhancing Grounding with Adaptive Region Perception for GUI Agents
papers.abstract: Existing GUI grounding methods often struggle with fine-grained localization in high-resolution screenshots. To address this, we propose GUI-ARP, a novel framework that enables adaptive multi-stage inference. Equipped with the proposed Adaptive Region Perception (ARP) and Adaptive Stage Controlling (ASC), GUI-ARP dynamically exploits visual attention for cropping task-relevant regions and adapts its inference strategy, performing a single-stage inference for simple cases and a multi-stage analysis for more complex scenarios. This is achieved through a two-phase training pipeline that integrates supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement fine-tuning based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). papers.title: Fractal Generative Distillation
alternate_titles: Fractal Generative Distillation
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation enables the deployment of high-performance deep neural networks on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact students. However, existing methods struggle with significant architecture heterogeneity and capacity gaps, often requiring careful feature alignment or auxiliary training objectives. We present Fractal Generative Distillation (FGD), a novel framework that reimagines knowledge transfer through the lens of hierarchical pattern generation. Our key insight is that teacher knowledge can be decomposed into self-similar fractal patterns that naturally bridge dimensional mismatches while preserving multi-scale structural information. FGD employs a generative diffusion process to synthesize these patterns conditioned on student features, enabling flexible knowledge transfer without explicit architectural constraints....

papers.title: Fourier Pruning for Large Language Models Compression
alternate_titles: Fourier Pruning for Large Language Models Compression
papers.abstract: We propose Fourier Pruning (FP), a novel post-training pruning method for Large Language Models (LLMs) that leverages frequency domain analysis to identify and remove redundant weights. Unlike existing methods that rely solely on magnitude or gradient-based metrics in the spatial domain, we transform weight matrices and their corresponding activations into the frequency domain using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Our key insight is that high-frequency components in neural network weights often correspond to noise or less important features, while low-frequency components capture essential patterns. We introduce a frequency-aware pruning metric that combines spectral energy distribution with activation importance scores to achieve superior pruning decisions. papers.title: Fine-Tuning Large Multimodal Models for Automatic Pronunciation Assessment
alternate_titles: Fine-Tuning Large Multimodal Models for Automatic Pronunciation Assessment
papers.abstract: Automatic Pronunciation Assessment (APA) is critical for Computer-Assisted Language Learning (CALL), requiring evaluation across multiple granularities and aspects. Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) present new opportunities for APA, but their effectiveness in fine-grained assessment remains uncertain. This work investigates fine-tuning LMMs for APA using the Speechocean762 dataset and a private corpus. Fine-tuning significantly outperforms zero-shot settings and achieves competitive results on single-granularity tasks compared to public and commercial systems. The model performs well at word and sentence levels, while phoneme-level assessment remains challenging. papers.title: Fine-Grained Text-to-Image Synthesis with Semantic Refinement
alternate_titles: Fine-Grained Text-to-Image Synthesis with Semantic Refinement
papers.abstract: Recent advance in text-to-image synthesis greatly benefits from large-scale vision-language models such as CLIP. Despite the capability of producing high-quality and creative images, existing methods often struggle in capturing details of the text prompt, especially when the text is lengthy. We reveal that such an issue is partially caused by the imperfect text-image matching using CLIP, where fine-grained semantics may get obscured by the dominant ones. This work presents a new diffusion-based method that favors fine-grained synthesis with semantic refinement. Concretely, instead of getting a synthesis using the entire descriptive sentence as the prompt, users can emphasize some specific words of their own interests. For this purpose, we incorporate a semantic-induced gradient as a reference input in each denoising step to help the model understand the selected sub-concept. We find out....

papers.title: FinMCP-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Real-World Financial Tool Use Under the Model Context Protocol
alternate_titles: FinMCP-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Real-World Financial Tool Use Under the Model Context Protocol
papers.abstract: This paper introduces FinMCP-Bench, a novel benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in solving real-world financial problems through tool invocation of financial model context protocols. FinMCP-Bench contains 613 samples spanning 10 main scenarios and 33 sub-scenarios, featuring both real and synthetic user queries to ensure diversity and authenticity. It incorporates 65 real financial MCPs and three types of samples, single tool, multi-tool, and multi-turn, allowing evaluation of models across different levels of task complexity. Using this benchmark, we systematically assess a range of mainstream LLMs and propose metrics that explicitly measure tool invocation accuracy and reasoning capabilities. FinMCP-Bench provides a standardized, practical, and challenging testbed for advancing research on financial LLM agents, and all resources will be publicly available at https://g...

papers.title: FedLA: Filter-Wise Learnable Aggregation for Federated Learning under non-IID Data
alternate_titles: FedLA: Filter-Wise Learnable Aggregation for Federated Learning under non-IID Data
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous client data distributions are a core challenge in federated learning, leading to severe local model divergence and degraded global performance. In this paper, we propose FedLA, a fine-grained filter-level learnable aggregation method, to address this challenge. It assigns an independent, learnable aggregation weight to each filter of the convolution layers, enabling flexible adjustment of each filter’s contribution to the global model. Specifically, the aggregation weights at each layer are packaged as a lightweight point-wise convolution module that is temporarily inserted during aggregation. Once trained, the modules are fused into the original convolution layers to complete the filter-wise aggregation. Experimental results show that this fine-grained learnable approach outperforms prior methods, improving the global model accuracy by up to 4.91%.

papers.title: FAST-GS: Frequency Aware Space-time Gaussian Splatting for Photorealistic Dynamic Novel View Synthesis

FAST-GS: Frequency Aware Space-Time Gaussian Splatting for Photorealistic Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
papers.abstract: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) excels in dynamic 3D reconstruction and real-time novel view synthesis via efficient 4D Gaussian representations and parallelizable rendering. However, existing 4DGS approaches rely on a single polynomial to model motion, which limits performance in complex dynamic scenes where high-frequency motion components are prevalent, and fails to ensure long-term stability due to cumulative trajectory drift. To address these issues, we propose a Fourier Motion Modeling module: this paradigm decomposes motion into frequency-based sinusoidal components, capturing both low-frequency global trajectories and high-frequency local details to model complex motion patterns accurately. It retains the real-time rendering capability of 4DGS while improving complex motion fitting and long-term coherence. Additionally, we integrate a motion-aware regularization strategy into the lo...

papers.title: FANSR: Frequency Adaptive Network for Efficient Image Super-Resolution
alternate_titles: FANSR: Frequency Adaptive Network for Efficient Image Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Transformer models have advanced single image super-resolution (SISR), but most emphasize enlarging the receptive field while underusing high-frequency cues across spatial and channel dimensions. To mitigate this self-attention(SA)’s low-pass bias, We propose FANSR (Frequency Adaptive Network for Efficient Image Super Resolution), a lightweight framework that considering receptive-field expansion with explicit high-frequency modeling. FANSR introduces two frequency-based token mixers that transform features into frequency representations along spatial and channel axes, efficiently isolating high-frequency components and injecting them as sparse priors into the subsequent Self-Attention block. We further introduce a Frequency Enhancement Loss (FE-Loss) that adaptively prioritizes high-frequency regions, enabled by the model’s explicit distinction of low- and high-frequency content. alternate_titles: F5E-TTS: Enhancing Speech Synthesis by Aligning Text with Rich Semantic Representations
papers.abstract: Mainstream Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems still struggle with semantic alignment between speech and text, resulting in unnatural or incorrect speech for some hard cases, a limitation we attribute to the semantic sparsity of text. To address this, we introduce F5E-TTS, a novel flow-matching framework that enriches the synthesis process by conditioning on both text and semantically dense PPG embeddings, the bottleneck features from a Phonetic PosteriorGrams (PPG) model. The core of our framework is a training strategy where a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone learns to implicitly align text and PPGs, further encouraged by an explicit cross-modal regularization technique using a shared vector-quantized (VQ) codebook. This enriched content representation generates more natural-sounding speech and significantly improves content accuracy. Our model achieves a state-of-the-art 16.4% relative W...

papers.title: Exploring SSL Discrete Tokens for Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition
alternate_titles: Exploring SSL Discrete Tokens for Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition
papers.abstract: With the advancement of self-supervised learning (SSL) in speech-related tasks, there has been growing interest in using discrete tokens generated by SSL models for automatic speech recognition (ASR) due to their potential for more efficient processing. However, previous studies have primarily focused on applying discrete tokens to English ASR, leaving a gap in their adaptation for multilingual ASR tasks. To address this, we present a systematic investigation into the use of SSL-generated discrete tokens for the Zipformer-Transducer ASR system across seven non-English languages and further incorporate cross-utterance speech context modelling. Experiments on the Multilingual Librispeech corpus demonstrate that discrete tokens outperform FBank features, achieving an average word error rate (WER) reduction of up to 0.45% and 1.86% absolute (4.20% and 16.83% relative) on the development and....

papers.title: Explore Like Humans: Autonomous Exploration with Online SG-Memo Construction for Embodied Agents
alternate_titles: Explore Like Humans: Autonomous Exploration with Online SG-Memo Construction for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Constructing structured spatial memory is essential for enabling long-horizon reasoning in complex embodied navigation tasks. Current memory construction predominantly relies on a decoupled, two-stage paradigm: agents first aggregate environmental data through exploration, followed by the offline reconstruction of spatial memory. However, this post-hoc and geometry-centric approach precludes agents from leveraging high-level semantic intelligence, often causing them to overlook navigationally critical landmarks (e.g., doorways and staircases) that serve as fundamental semantic anchors in human cognitive maps. To bridge this gap, we propose ABot-Explorer, a novel active exploration framework that unifies memory construction and exploration into an online, RGB-only process. At its core, ABot-Explorer leverages Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to distill Semantic Navigational Affordances...

papers.title: Exploiting intra-core heterogeneity for high-performance dense linear algebra on Huawei Ascend 910 NPUs
alternate_titles: Exploiting intra-core heterogeneity for high-performance dense linear algebra on Huawei Ascend 910 NPUs
papers.abstract: Dense linear algebra kernels—General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM), Triangular Solve with Multiple Right-Hand Sides (TRSM), and LU decomposition with partial pivoting (GETRF)—serve as foundational computational building blocks for both High-Performance Computing (HPC) and modern Artificial Intelligence (AI). While highly optimized implementations exist for CPUs and GPUs, emerging Neural Processing Units (NPUs) present unique architectural challenges that demand novel algorithmic approaches to achieve peak performance. The Huawei Ascend 910 NPU exemplifies these challenges: each of its 20 AI cores integrates heterogeneous functional units (Cube, Vector, Scalar) capable of concurrent execution. papers.title: Experience-Driven Dynamic Exits for LLMs with Reinforcement Learning
alternate_titles: Experience-Driven Dynamic Exits for LLMs with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Large Language Models suffer from slow autoregressive inference. While self-speculative decoding accelerates this process, its efficiency is hampered by static configurations like fixed exit layers and speculation lengths. We reframe this optimization as a \textbf{Markov Decision Process} and propose \textbf{LEDE}, a framework that uses offline reinforcement learning. LEDE learns a policy to dynamically select the optimal exit layer and speculation length based on the local context of the generated sequence at each step, balancing computational cost and draft quality. Comprehensive evaluations on Llama-2 and Llama-3 models show LEDE achieves up to a $2.0\times$$\sim$$2.7\times$ speedup over autoregressive decoding and and provides an additional 17\% speedup over the static speculative baselines.

papers.title: Evaluating ASR-LLM Setups for Japanese Speech Recognition with Multi-Pass Augmented Generative Error Correction
alternate_titles: Evaluating ASR-LLM Setups for Japanese Speech Recognition with Multi-Pass Augmented Generative Error Correction
papers.abstract: With the strong representational power of large language models (LLMs), generative error correction (GER) for automatic speech recognition (ASR) aims to provide semantic and phonetic refinements to address ASR errors. This work explores how LLM-based GER can enhance and expand the capabilities of Japanese ASR, providing a systematic evaluation on Japanese data with 0.9-2.6k text utterances. We also introduce a new multi-pass augmented generative error correction (MPA GER) by integrating multiple system hypotheses on the input side with corrections from multiple LLMs on the output side and then merging them. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first investigation of the use of LLMs for Japanese GER, which involves second-pass language modeling on the output transcriptions generated by the ASR system (e.g., N-best hypotheses). Our experiments demonstrated performance improvement in t...

papers.title: Equipping Large Language Model with Directional Speech Understanding Capabilities
alternate_titles: Equipping Large Language Model with Directional Speech Understanding Capabilities
papers.abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated that prompting large language models (LLM) with audio encodings enables effective speech understanding capabilities. However, most speech LLMs are trained on single-channel, single-talker data, which makes it challenging to directly apply them to multi-talker and multi-channel speech understanding task. In this work, we present a comprehensive investigation on how to enable directional multi-talker speech understanding capabilities for LLMs, specifically in smart glasses usecase. We propose two novel approaches to integrate directivity into LLMs: (1) a cascaded system that leverages a source separation frontend module, and (2) an end-to-end system that utilizes serialized output training. All of the approaches utilize a multi-microphone array embedded in smart glasses to optimize directivity interpretation and processing in a streaming manner. Experimenta...

papers.title: Enhancing Cross-Subject Generalization for Selective Auditory Attention Decoding Via Multi-Expert Voting
alternate_titles: Enhancing Cross-Subject Generalization for Selective Auditory Attention Decoding Via Multi-Expert Voting
papers.abstract: Selective Auditory Attention Decoding (AAD) aims to identify the direction of the attended speaker from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals in multi-speaker scenarios. However, existing AAD methods often struggle to generalize to unseen subjects. For the ICASSP 2026 EEG-AAD Challenge, a multi-expert voting strategy, which integrates several state-of-the-art (SOTA) neural networks (NNs) and aggregates predictions from diverse architectures, effectively reducing single-model bias and improving performance and robustness, is proposed. Additionally, direct current (DC) drift removal, rereferencing, and bandpass filter are applied to preprocess the EEG signals. The proposed strategies rank first in track 1 of the EEG-AAD Challenge, achieving an average decoding accuracy of 56.5% on unseen subjects.

papers.title: Enhancing Audio Question-Answering Performance Through Log-Likelihood Guided Reward Functions
alternate_titles: Enhancing Audio Question-Answering Performance Through Log-Likelihood Guided Reward Functions
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has shown promise in training Large Language Models (LLMs) for text-to-text and multimodal tasks. Current RLVR approaches for audio question-answering often use format adherence and binary correctness signals. We propose a new reward framework for extracting learning signals from multiple-choice questions (MCQs). Our approach uses probability-ratio rewards to increase the likelihood difference between correct and incorrect answer choices, expanding beyond accuracy metrics. We conducted experiments on a standard audio-reasoning benchmark, where our probability-ratio reward framework performed better than the base model and existing RLVR methods. The results suggest that likelihood-based rewards can improve audio reasoning capabilities, offering an enhanced approach for multiple-choice audio question-answering systems. Specifically, we....

papers.title: Emotional Damage: Investigating Safety Vulnerabilities of Large Audio-Language Models Under Speaker Emotional Variations
alternate_titles: Emotional Damage: Investigating Safety Vulnerabilities of Large Audio-Language Models Under Speaker Emotional Variations
papers.abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) extend text-based LLMs with auditory understanding, offering new opportunities for multimodal applications. While their perception, reasoning, and task performance have been widely studied, their safety alignment under paralinguistic variation remains underexplored. This work systematically investigates the role of speaker emotion. We construct a dataset of malicious speech instructions expressed across multiple emotions and intensities, and evaluate several state-of-the-art LALMs. Our results reveal substantial safety inconsistencies: different emotions elicit varying levels of unsafe responses, and the effect of intensity is non-monotonic, with medium expressions often posing the greatest risk. These findings highlight an overlooked vulnerability in LALMs and call for alignment strategies explicitly designed to ensure robustness under emotional varia...

papers.title: Efficient Distillation of Large Language Models Using Group Relative Policy Distillation
alternate_titles: Efficient Distillation of Large Language Models Using Group Relative Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: We present Group Relative Policy Distillation (GRPD), a novel knowledge distillation framework that addresses the computational challenges of deploying large language models in resource-constrained environments. Our approach reformulates knowledge distillation as a group-wise optimization problem, where we dynamically adjust the distillation process based on relative performance metrics across different sample groups. We introduce a Pearson distance-based distillation loss function that captures the correlation structure between teacher and student model outputs, providing more nuanced knowledge transfer compared to traditional KL divergence methods. papers.title: E2E-AEC: Implementing An End-To-End Neural Network Learning Approach for Acoustic Echo Cancellation

papers.abstract: We propose a novel neural network-based end-to-end acoustic echo cancellation (E2E-AEC) method capable of streaming inference, which operates effectively without reliance on traditional linear AEC (LAEC) techniques and time delay estimation. Our approach includes several key strategies: First, we introduce and refine progressive learning to gradually enhance echo suppression. Second, our model employs knowledge transfer by initializing with a pre-trained LAEC-based model, harnessing the insights gained from LAEC training. Third, we optimize the attention mechanism with a loss function applied on attention weights to achieve precise time alignment between the reference and microphone signals. Lastly, we incorporate voice activity detection to enhance speech quality and improve echo removal by masking the network output when near-end speech is absent.
